topPains.whyHighest: This is the track scope verbatim ('transform public data into actionable municipal priorities'), named by officer, councillor and journalist at sev4-5/freq4-5. Twenty reports of one flooded street show as twenty tickets, not one high-priority problem; officers triage by gut and by whichever councillor called last, and cannot answer 'top 3 priorities this week' with data. TN's new mandatory monthly grievance reports (Chief-Secretary push) make a defensible ranked list an immediate institutional need. Embedding-based clustering + a severity/volume/recurrence/aging score is a clean 36hr dashboard demo and the literal deliverable judges will look for.
topPains.solutionDirection: De-dupe across channels via location+issue embedding similarity, cluster into single 'problems', score each on safety/health keywords, affected-population (report count), recurrence and age-past-SLA, and render a ranked ward dashboard. Same pipeline auto-generates the monthly resolution/aging report that councillor/MLA offices now compile by hand — prioritization and accountability reporting from one structured store.

topPains.whyHighest: Strong, evidence-backed differentiator flagged by both the ward officer and the citizen (sev4-5/freq3-4). Closure-target pressure plus the 30-day timer drives false closures (photo from another street, 'forwarded = done'); citizens re-file, escalate, trust collapses. Documented for Namma Chennai ('closed within 24 hours without resolution') and Andhra PGRS (only 22% satisfaction on 'resolved' cases; DARPG now bars premature closure). This is the insight that elevates a generic dashboard: rank wards by REAL unresolved load, not the official 'resolved' count that hides the backlog — a memorable demo and a credible pilot pitch. Anomaly-flagging is buildable in 36hr; the citizen photo/callback verification is the production phase.
topPains.solutionDirection: Anomaly layer over closure metadata: flag closures that are suspiciously fast (<24h), lack a valid before/after geotagged proof photo, or re-file at the same location within N days. Recompute a 'true unresolved load' per ward that discounts likely-false closures, and gate closure on lightweight citizen-callback/photo verification in production.

Kept in scope by grounding strictly in NHM/RCH protocols and outputting escalation guidance, not diagnoses.
topPains.solutionDirection: A retrieval-grounded Tamil assistant over NHM/RCH/triage protocols (Gemini + a curated protocol corpus, with expert-escalation for low-confidence answers, ASHABot-style). result.track: AI for Sustainable Cities & Climate Action (SDG 11 & 13)

topPains.title: Ward/lane-level predictive heatwave alerts driven by a heat-vulnerability index
topPains.whyHighest: The single strongest cluster: 4 pains across every persona (CCMC crews, urban resident, TNPCB officer, basti resident), scoring sev5/ai5/build5 and mapping to the literal named example build 'predictive heatwave alerts'. The gap is real and evidenced: IMD/state alerts are one district-wide number while UHI adds 3-7C ward-to-ward, HeatWatch found alerts in only 5 of 13 death locations (2024-25), TN notified heatwave a state disaster with Rs 4 lakh relief, and Coimbatore faces 200-250 discomfort-days by 2050. All input data is open (IMD/ERA5 forecasts, LST/NDVI satellite, census density/income), so no hardware and no municipal telemetry is needed - a genuine 36hr build with an immediate single-ULB pilot.

Adds a municipal action layer: flag which wards to shift labour hours today and where to open cooling shelters. Pilotable by overlaying one corporation's ward map; low-bandwidth SMS fallback for low-end Android.

topPains.title: Neighborhood pollution map from sparse stations + low-cost-sensor calibration
topPains.whyHighest: 5 pains converge here and it is the track's core named deliverable ('neighborhood-level pollution mapping from open sensor data'). Two sub-pains fuse cleanly: the interpolation model AND the ML calibration layer that corrects low-cost-sensor humidity/heat drift against reference stations - the enabler that makes cheap coverage decision-grade (proven in Lucknow/Kanpur/Bhubaneswar). topPains.solutionDirection: Model that fuses the 3 reference stations + satellite AOD + optional calibrated low-cost-sensor readings into a live ward-resolution PM2.5/AQI surface with source-hotspot attribution (transport dust, cement, open burning). Bundle the calibration model so community/NGO sensors become trusted inputs. Citizen side: personal-exposure and safe-route/safe-hour advice in Tamil; regulator side: the spatial picture to act on and defend decisions. 36hr demo uses open NAMP feeds for one city with a synthetic-then-real calibration path.

topPains.title: Tamil AI civic-grievance layer that predicts sewage-overflow and street-flood risk hotspots
topPains.whyHighest: The highest-buildability cluster (build5/freq5) and the connective tissue for the whole platform - 5 pains fold in: sewage complaints arriving on paper too late (CCMC), grievances falsely marked 'resolved' (resident), paper/silo case records (TNPCB), and both recurring-flood pains where the same waterlogging spots submerge yearly. Pure software on data that already exists (complaints, DEM, rainfall nowcast) - the strongest 36hr demo with clear before/after accountability value.
topPains.solutionDirection: PWA with Tamil voice/photo intake that auto-geotags and classifies complaints, clusters duplicates into recurring blockage/waterlogging hotspots, and predicts high-risk manholes/junctions and low-lying streets before monsoon (complaint history + DEM/elevation + rainfall nowcast). Closes the loop with a before/after-photo + GPS verification step that flags premature 'resolved' closures, turning citizen reports into a live civic-risk map and a pre-emptive crew worklist / drain-desilting priority list.

topPains.title: Satellite-driven inspection triage: ranked daily worklist for the overloaded regulator
topPains.whyHighest: A distinct, defensible opportunity (TNPCB sev5/freq4/ai4/build4) with a different data source and user than the citizen map, and a uniquely strong pilot hook: enforcement today is 100% reactive - a complaint arrives, weeks pass, staff drive out and place 9 instruments after the kiln has fired. 100+ unregistered Thadagam kilns, 185 declared illegal, mining continued until a 2025 Madras HC-ordered SIT, and >50% of SPCB posts are vacant, so one officer with one vehicle cannot prioritize. It converts the pollution map into action and rides open satellite thermal-anomaly data (no ground hardware), making it credibly buildable and instantly valuable to a partner already under court pressure.
topPains.solutionDirection: Layer on the pollution map: detect brick-kiln firing and industrial thermal/smoke anomalies from open satellite feeds, cross the signal with hotspot AQI and complaint density, and output a ranked 'inspect these units this week' worklist for the officer's single field team. Auto-draft the geotagged, deduplicated case record (complaint -> location -> measurement -> notice -> outcome) so the compliance trail a court demands is queryable, cutting the reporting overhead that keeps skeleton staff out of the field.

result.oneLiner: A Tamil-first PWA that turns a city heatwave warning into a named, ranked "check on these people today" worklist for the ward health worker, grounded in NDMA heat-illness protocol.
result.pain: On red/orange heat days, IMD/city alerts are broadcast to everyone at once, so nobody acts on any single person. Meanwhile the ASHA/anganwadi/ward-health worker who does home visits has no way to know WHICH of her elderly, pregnant, infant, cardiac/renal, or outdoor-worker cases sit in the hottest, least-shaded lanes and need a visit or call today. Heat deaths are silent, undercounted, and hit the same vulnerable households the worker already knows by name — but she is paper-bound and blind to the heat-island geography layered on top of her caseload.

result.angle: Frontline-worker tool: person-resolution, not ward-resolution. Instead of one more color-coded map, it fuses the ward heat-vulnerability layer with the worker's OWN registry of vulnerable individuals and hands her a short, ordered field worklist plus a spoken Tamil triage script — the broadcast warning becomes accountable, name-level action she completes on a low-end phone.

One-tap Tamil heat-illness triage: guided spoken symptom check (heat cramp vs exhaustion vs stroke) that outputs escalate-to-108 / cool-and-rehydrate / advise, grounded in NDMA + clinical protocol via RAG
Voice visit-logging: worker speaks the outcome in Tamil (Bhashini ASR); auto-structured into the case record, closing the loop and feeding a live 'who's still unchecked' view

Municipal rollup: ward-level heatmap of unreached high-risk cases + a ranked 'open cooling shelter here / shift labour hours in these wards today' brief for the officer, with low-bandwidth SMS fallback

Bhashini Tamil TTS + ASR — spoken advisories for low-literacy households and hands-free Tamil voice visit-logging; the govt-backed Indian-language stack, not English-only cloud speech
Gemini vision — reads dwelling roof/ventilation from a registration photo to auto-fill a housing heat-risk factor, and can flag visible heat-illness signs
RAG over NDMA Heat Action Plan guidelines + heat-illness clinical management protocol — so every triage/advisory is grounded and defensible to the health officer, not hallucinated

result.pain: A Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board (TNPCB) regional office runs a skeleton field team against hundreds of units — brick kilns, dyeing/cement/foundry units, open-burning sites. They cannot inspect everywhere, so targeting is ad-hoc and complaint-driven, and reactive. Worse, the paperwork burden (compiling geotagged evidence, drafting notices citing the exact rule, maintaining a trail a green tribunal will accept) keeps the few staff at their desks instead of in the field. Signals that already exist — CPCB station AQI, satellite smoke/thermal, citizen complaints — sit in three disconnected silos and never become a prioritized action list.

result.angle: Official / admin intelligence: not another citizen AQI app (SAMEER already does that), but the enforcement action layer sitting on top of the pollution map — turning messy multi-source field signal into a ranked, defensible worklist and removing the reporting overhead that keeps skeleton staff off the field.

Satellite anomaly layer: Gemini-vision flags active brick-kiln firing and industrial thermal/smoke plumes on open Sentinel-2 / thermal tiles, pinned to unit locations

One-click case record: on inspect/act, auto-compiles a geotagged, deduplicated evidence stack (signal -> location -> measurement -> photos) into a queryable, NGT-defensible record
RAG-cited draft notice generator: produces the show-cause / closure notice quoting the specific Air Act / TNPCB rule violated, in Tamil + English, as an editable PDF
aiComponents: Gemini 2.x multimodal vision — classify satellite thermal/smoke anomalies (kiln firing signatures, plume presence) and triage citizen complaint photos; chosen because it needs zero training data and reasons over heterogeneous image tiles fast in a 36hr window

RAG over TNPCB / CPCB regulation corpus (Air Act 1981, Water Act, board directions) — grounds the auto-drafted notice's legal citations so they are real and quotable, not hallucinated; RAG specifically because a wrong rule citation is legally fatal
Bhashini Tamil ASR/TTS — Tamil voice complaint intake for citizens and a spoken Tamil worklist + notice readout for the field team on low-end Android
Spatial interpolation model (IDW/kriging) fusing reference stations + satellite AOD into the ward AQI surface — lightweight, explainable, defensible before a regulator
result.mvp36hr: One city (Coimbatore). Overlay the corporation ward map, ingest open CPCB/NAMP station feeds for AQI, pull one satellite AOD + thermal tile set, and load a synthetic-then-real complaint set. GDG Coimbatore for technical enablement (satellite tile pipeline, Bhashini integration); Startup Culture for the corporation MoU and incubation. Scale framework: same fusion engine re-points to any board's station feeds + ward map, so a win in Coimbatore templates to any TN corporation.

Legal sensitivity — the auto-drafted notice stays a draft-for-officer-sign, never auto-issued; wrong RAG citations create liability, so it is explicitly human-in-the-loop
Adoption — overloaded officers reject tools that add clicks; value must be net-negative paperwork time, so case-record auto-fill must genuinely replace manual compilation
Data access — real TNPCB unit registry and inspection history is hard to get pre-MoU; MVP leans on open CPCB feeds + a synthetic unit list

result.name: MaruthuVaani
result.track: AI for Good Health & Well-being
result.oneLiner: Snap your handwritten prescription and MaruthuVaani reads it back to you in plain Tamil — with a picture dose-card and voice reminders — so a patient who can't read still takes the right medicine at the right time.
result.pain: The doctor/PHC visit is the easy part; the last mile is where health collapses. In rural TN, a large share of patients (elderly, low-literacy women, farm labourers) leave the PHC/pharmacy with a handwritten prescription they physically cannot read. They can't tell the BP tablet from the antibiotic, don't know 'twice daily after food', stop the course when they feel better, and re-take or over-dose. Existing 'health apps' are English, text-first, urban, and diagnosis-focused — none solve 'I am holding a paper I can't read.' The result is medication errors, wasted PHC re-visits, and avoidable admissions — exactly the resource-constrained-setting burden this track targets.
result.whoUses: The patient or their family caregiver directly — a low-literacy, Tamil-first, low-end-Android user (elderly NCD patient, pregnant woman, parent of a sick child, farm/daily-wage worker). Also usable by the PHC pharmacist/ASHA who generates the dose-card for the patient at discharge.
result.angle: End-user / citizen tool: a phone-first Tamil audio+pictogram companion the patient uses on their own device, in scope as it 'assists healthcare workers in resource-constrained settings' by closing the post-consult adherence gap the PHC can't staff.
coreFeatures: Snap-to-understand: photo of a handwritten or printed Rx -> Gemini Vision OCR -> structured {drug, dose, timing, food, duration, purpose} that the app reads aloud in plain Tamil
Pictographic dose-card for non-readers: each medicine as a coloured pill icon + sun/noon/moon + rice-bowl (before/after food) grid, printable/screenshot-able, no words needed
Offline Tamil voice + visual reminders at each dose time ('unga BP marundhu neram, saapaattukku appuram') with a big one-tap 'taken' button, streak tracking for the full course
Grounded safety layer: every reading shows the original Rx crop next to it, flags unreadable/ambiguous items as 'ask the pharmacist' instead of guessing, and never invents a dose
Danger-sign voice check: patient speaks a symptom in Tamil (ASR), RAG over NHM/RCH red-flag protocols returns refer-now vs watch-at-home with a citation and 'go to PHC' one-tap
aiComponents: Gemini 2.x Flash Vision — OCR + structuring of messy handwritten/printed prescriptions into typed fields; vision (not plain OCR) because it reasons over layout, abbreviations (OD/BD/TDS, HS, a/c) and doctor shorthand

RAG over a curated Indian drug formulary + NHM/RCH protocol corpus — grounds drug-name normalization, 'what is it for' in plain Tamil, and the red-flag triage; prevents dosage/diagnosis hallucination and yields citations
Bhashini (IndicTTS) Tamil TTS — govt-backed rural-Tamil voice for dose explanations and reminders; audio is generated once and cached on-device so playback works fully offline
Bhashini Tamil ASR — patient speaks symptoms/questions for the danger-sign check on low-literacy input
Gemini for plain-Tamil simplification — turns 'Amlodipine 5mg OD' into 'the small white BP tablet, one every morning after food', constrained to the RAG-retrieved facts
result.mvp36hr: Build ONLY the snap-to-Tamil-dose-card path: React PWA where the user photographs a prescription -> Gemini Vision returns structured meds -> RAG normalizes names + purpose -> render the pictographic dose-card AND play Bhashini Tamil audio per medicine -> schedule local (offline) reminders with a 'taken' button. Ship 6-8 real sample Tamil-Nadu Rx images (handwritten + printed) hard-tested. Skip full ASR triage, ABHA linking, and multi-user sync for the demo.
result.differentiator: Every other entrant will build a symptom-checker or a chatbot. This is the only tool aimed at the moment a patient holds a paper they can't read — prescription comprehension for the illiterate, not diagnosis. It is voice+picture-first (zero reading required), grounded and safety-framed (shows the original crop, defers instead of guessing a dose), and works offline after one capture. That combination — post-consult adherence, low-literacy, offline Tamil audio — is essentially unserved.
result.pilotPath: Pilot at one NHM-TN block: PHC pharmacist/ASHA generates the dose-card at dispensing, patient walks out with audio + reminders on their own or family phone. Measure course-completion and re-visit reduction over a cohort. TiE Kovai for clinician validation of the safety guardrails; GDG for Bhashini/ABDM integration; position as an adherence add-on to e-Sanjeevani spokes and later link to ABHA for a longitudinal med record. Incubation: patient-adherence layer licensable to state health missions and telemedicine providers (a telemedicine company-style).
risks: Handwritten-Rx OCR accuracy is the core technical risk — illegible doctor handwriting can be misread; mitigate by always showing the original crop, confidence-flagging, and deferring ambiguous items to the pharmacist rather than guessing
Patient-safety/liability: a misread dose can harm; must be framed as a reading-aid not medical advice, never fabricate a dose, and keep a human (pharmacist/ASHA) confirmation step in the pilot
Bhashini API reliability and rural-Tamil TTS naturalness; mitigate by caching generated audio on-device and having a fallback voice
Adoption: some patients lack a smartphone — relies on family/caregiver phone or PHC-generated card, so reach is via the caregiver, not always the patient
Prescription formats vary wildly (paper, thermal print, scheme cards); need a curated TN sample set to avoid overfitting the demo

# VeppaNadi — Build Spec
*Track: AI for Sustainable Cities & Climate Action · Tag: Best Domain Fit*

**Pitch** — A Tamil-first ward-level heatwave early-warning PWA whose vulnerability index is calibrated by live, de-identified telemedicine consult signals — a self-tuning "health-adjusted heat risk" map that proves interventions worked.

**Pain + evidence** — Every heat-action dashboard predicts *exposure* (temp, land-surface-temp, tree cover); none see the *health outcome*. A corporation's heat cell fires one city-wide alert whether a ward is a green enclave or a treeless slum where auto-drivers are collapsing. India's 2024 heat season logged 40,000+ suspected heat-stroke cases and 100+ deaths (NCDC/MoHFW), yet ward-level morbidity stays invisible until hospital admissions confirm it — after the intervention window (shift labour to dawn, open a shelter) has closed.

**Who + core loop** — Corporation Heat Action Plan cell / ward health officers (Coimbatore pilot). Loop: environmental HVI → re-weighted by observed heat-illness consult rate per ward → ranked "shift hours / open shelter here today" worklist → after action, track the ward's consult-curve to prove the morbidity line bent.

**AI stack** — Gemini as a Tamil/English syndromic classifier (chief-complaint notes → heat-exhaustion/dehydration/COPD categories → per-ward signal); Gemini grounded generation for exposure-specific Tamil advisories; RAG over the city Heat Action Plan + NDMA/IMD guidelines so every recommendation is citeable; Bhashini Tamil TTS/ASR; raster pipeline aggregating satellite LST/NDVI to ward polygons.

**36hr MVP slice** — One live Coimbatore ward map: pre-baked LST/NDVI + IMD/ERA5 forecast = base HVI; Gemini classifies a seeded set of Tamil complaint notes into per-ward heat-illness counts to compute the health-adjusted re-ranking. Ship three things only: (1) RAG-cited action worklist, (2) one Bhashini Tamil voice + SMS advisory for the top ward, (3) before/after consult-curve panel. React PWA, installable on a low-end phone.

**90-sec wow** — Toggle "environmental-only" vs "health-adjusted" — wards visibly re-rank; play the Tamil voice advisory; show the consult curve bending after a shelter opens.

**Pilot/incubation** — DPDP-compliant k-anonymized ward counts from an a telemedicine company-style partner; TiE Kovai connects the corporation heat cell; GDG for Bhashini/satellite enablement. Phase 1: one zone + SMS. Phase 2: city-wide proof-of-impact dashboard the state cell can fund. Exit: B2G SaaS licensing the health-adjusted HVI.

**Why it wins / risks** — Moat is the data partnership, not the model: anyone scrapes IMD; nobody without a consult stream calibrates against real ward-resolved morbidity. Risks: consult surges reflect care-seeking not incidence (needs access normalization); sparse rural wards need min-count smoothing; real data feed requires a signed DPDP path judges will probe.

# PayirDesk — Build Spec

**Pitch:** A Tamil-first triage cockpit that lets one block Agricultural Officer supervise AI across 1,100+ farms — auto-closing routine leaf cases, surfacing only ranked, outbreak-clustered escalations.

**Pain + evidence:** One TN Assistant Agricultural Officer (AAO) covers 1,100+ farms and drowns in one-off leaf queries, so advice arrives late and farmers self-medicate with wrong pesticide doses. India's farm advisory ratio runs ~1 extension worker per 1,000+ farmers (well past FAO's recommended ~1:400), leaving most smallholders to guess. Farmer apps dump raw AI diagnoses with no officer loop and no dose check.

**Who + core loop:** Primary user = block AAO. Intake = smallholder farmers. Loop: farmer snaps a leaf photo + asks in Tamil (WhatsApp/PWA) → Gemini vision pre-diagnoses with a confidence flag → high-confidence common cases auto-resolve with a TNAU-grounded, correctly-dosed Tamil remedy (voice + text) → low-confidence/high-stakes cases enter the officer's de-duplicated, ranked queue → cases cluster by disease+block+week to flag outbreaks early.

**AI stack:** Gemini 2.0 Flash vision (cheap, fast multimodal, tolerates low-res field photos) · RAG over TNAU Crop Protection / Package of Practices (grounds exact, verifiable dose — safety-critical) · Bhashini Tamil TTS/ASR (free, govt-backed, best Tamil, aligns with incubation path) · deterministic count-based clustering over disease+geo+time (trust + clean demo).

**36hr MVP slice:** Intake→triage only. PWA photo upload → Gemini diagnosis + confidence → high-confidence returns TNAU-grounded dosed Tamil remedy (text + Bhashini audio); low-confidence drops into the officer console as a ranked queue, clustered by disease+block so one seeded outbreak lights up. Cut: WhatsApp bot, insurance export, ASR follow-up.

**90-sec demo wow:** Officer dashboard clears 8 auto-resolved cases, actions 1 escalation, and catches a "14 blast cases in Pollachi this week" outbreak cluster before the block is lost.

**Pilot/incubation:** One block near GRD (Pollachi) with a single AAO + Farmer Field School, seeded via existing Uzhavagam reach. TiE Kovai validates TNAU dose KB; GDG enables Bhashini/Gemini; prove officer-time-saved + faster outbreak detection, then position as the officer-side layer atop TN's Uzhavan app, scaling on Bhashini's Indic stack.

**Why it wins / risks:** Only tool making the officer the *supervisor* of AI, not a leaf-by-leaf answerer — Plantix/Uzhavan hand raw diagnoses to farmers with no officer loop, dose grounding, or outbreak signal. Risks: dose liability (hard-cite TNAU, human-in-loop for all spray advice); vision accuracy on messy photos (conservative thresholds); Bhashini agri-dialect gaps; officer adoption (must save time day one); patchy 4G (graceful offline queueing).

# OruKural — Build Spec
*Track: AI for Good — Health & Well-being · Tag: Safest Bet*

**Pitch** — An ASHA/ANM speaks one Tamil sentence per patient; it fans out into every register summary plus government-app-ready payloads (HMIS/ANMOL/Ni-Kshay), offline-first.

**Pain + evidence** — Frontline health workers are the system's most over-documented staff: one encounter is hand-copied into 10-15 paper registers, then re-typed into ANMOL/RCH/HMIS/Ni-Kshay. Surveys peg **30-50% of an ANM's working hours on redundant recording, not care**. Rural TN worsens it — workers think in Tamil; the apps demand English, structured, online input on a low-end phone with patchy 4G.

**Who + core loop** — Rural TN ASHAs/ANMs/PHC nurses (consumed upward by PHC/Block MOs). Capture ONCE — speak or snap, in Tamil, offline → system fans out, dedups, exports so paper registers and govt apps agree by construction.

**AI stack** — Bhashini Tamil ASR (on-device Whisper-small Tamil offline fallback) → **Gemini 2.x Flash** structured extraction to strict typed JSON with per-field confidence (handles code-mixed Tanglish); Gemini vision OCR as alternate "snap the page" path; Bhashini Tamil TTS read-back for confirmation. Fan-out + export templating is **deterministic (non-AI)** — auditable numbers, no hallucinated reporting.

**36hr MVP slice** — ONE encounter type: ANC visit. Mic → one Tamil sentence → ASR → Gemini extracts {name, ANC visit#, gestational month, anaemia flag, next-visit}. Parsed card, TTS read-back, tap commit. Instantly populates ANC summary row + eligible-couple/RCH row + downloadable ANMOL/HMIS JSON+CSV. Nothing else.

**90-sec demo wow** — Speak one sentence → five artefacts appear. Flip to airplane mode, capture two more (queued), restore 4G, watch the sync queue drain. Capture-once → five outputs → offline→sync.

**Pilot path** — 3-5 sub-centres under one Coimbatore PHC block via TiE Kovai + District/Block MO; metric = documentation minutes saved/ANM/day + register-vs-app mismatch reduction over 6 weeks. Start CSV-only (no API approval needed); graduate to official HMIS/ANMOL push via NHM state IT cell. GDG for PWA hardening; Startup Culture for incubation/MoU.

**Track:** AI for Strong Institutions · **Tag:** Boldest

**Pitch:** A Tamil-first civic evidence layer that turns citizen before/after geotagged photos into a public-works ledger, then cross-checks it against municipal spend to expose ghost closures *and* ghost works — "money moved, ground unchanged."

# Sollu — Build Spec

**Pitch:** Speak a civic complaint in everyday Tamil; instantly get it back as a formal, correctly-routed petition with the responsible officer, legal deadline, and a tracking code.

**Pain + evidence:** Rural citizens can't draft the formal, department-specific petitions that govt systems expect, so grievances land in the wrong desk or get rejected on format. **36hr MVP slice:** ONE district, THREE departments (roads/water/sanitation). Voice-in → formal petition → officer + deadline + tracking code → SMS/shareable receipt. Skip auth, skip real govt API — log to Firestore, demo status lookup by code.

**90-sec demo wow:** Mentor speaks a messy Tamil pothole complaint; 8 seconds later Sollu speaks back a crisp petition, names the exact AE, "legal deadline: 15 days," and prints a QR tracking code.

**Pilot/incubation path:** Pilot via a TiE Kovai-linked ward councillor as a complaint intake desk; scale as a plug-in over CM Helpline / CPGRAMS.

**Why it wins / risks:** Wins on visceral voice demo + a real institutional gap. Risks: routing accuracy and official adoption — mitigate with human-in-loop confirmation and read-only pilot.
